nodes.title: Reviewed manifest and forecast-binding execution record
Recorded fixed graph-operation conformance
nodes.statement: The committed B2a run record documents local independent review and 26/26 synthetic API checks under graph-transformation-probes-v2. The fixed identity/projection implementation computes outputs and losses and rejects altered completion inputs. This is bounded local conformance, not arbitrary artifact execution, semantic equivalence, external witnessing or predictive advantage.

nodes.title: Embedded outputs and assessment costs have limited scope
nodes.statement: The B2a run record embeds generated graphs in completion events without materializing new representation or forecast manifests. Its elapsed time and zero program model calls/external spend cover assessment, not the full builder and reviewer effort. The retained record does not close either the output-consumer or whole-step cost gap.

nodes.title: Recorded assertion API conformance
nodes.statement: The committed A run record documents independent local review and a real assessment worker with 8/8 source-span and 6/6 assertion-history checks on synthetic ledgers. These are implementation contracts, not extraction truth, predictive improvement, deployment or independent timestamp assurance.

nodes.title: Recorded manifest and forecast-binding conformance
nodes.statement: The committed B1 run record documents independent local review and 22/22 actual manifest API checks under representation-manifest-probes-v2, including identity, input and supplied-forecast binding. The recorded worker queued transformations; this does not prove predictor execution, independently measured costs, transformation preservation or predictive advantage.

nodes.title: Operational meta-representation
nodes.statement: A meta-representation records representation families, permitted transformations, preservation obligations and comparative evidence.

nodes.title: Entityhood is representability
nodes.statement: The project convention defines an entity as anything representable, with persistence treated separately.

nodes.title: Entityhood as persistent fixed points
nodes.statement: The Lawvere note associates entities with persistent fixed points; this conflicts with the broader project convention.

nodes.title: Fixed-point hypotheses are required
nodes.statement: Lawvere fixed-point results do not establish dynamic attraction, conservation or mechanical structure without additional construction.

nodes.title: Prompt as Lagrangian
nodes.statement: A correspondence between prompt revision and Lagrangian dynamics is a hypothesis requiring operational variables and discriminating tests.

nodes.title: Construction of variables remains open
nodes.statement: The project has not derived a general procedure for choosing optimal state variables from observations.

nodes.title: Ledger preserves attributed representations
nodes.statement: The integrated ledger preserves directed typed relationships with evidence scoped to a selected snapshot.

nodes.title: Story parser is a mutable view
nodes.statement: The story parser uses names as relationship endpoints and time-dependent identifiers rather than an immutable assertion history.

nodes.title: Two time axes are necessary
nodes.statement: World-time claims and collection-time eligibility must remain separate to prevent retrospective knowledge leakage.

nodes.title: Newer information is not automatically true
nodes.statement: Preserve disagreement and corrections separately instead of making recency the scientific truth policy.

nodes.title: Graph usefulness depends on task and budget
nodes.statement: Graph retrieval should be compared with strong text retrieval at matched context and total construction costs.

nodes.title: Memory requires multiple tests
nodes.statement: Temporal reasoning, updates, abstention, environment experience and heterogeneous evidence require distinct evaluation tasks.

nodes.title: Graphiti is a candidate adapter
nodes.statement: Temporal graph and hybrid retrieval functionality can be evaluated behind an adapter while independent source history is retained.

nodes.title: Standards describe structure and provenance
nodes.statement: RDF, PROV-O, SHACL and nanopublications offer complementary interchange, provenance, validation and assertion packaging.

nodes.title: Selection must charge the interpreter
nodes.statement: Description-length comparison requires explicit coding and residual conventions, rather than measuring prompt length alone.

nodes.title: Reusable programs can change representation vocabulary
nodes.statement: Library learning is a concrete candidate mechanism for expanding the primitives used to express solutions.

nodes.title: Transformations need preservation contracts
nodes.statement: Type or semantic obligations can make schema migration accountable; canonical mappings need not be invertible.

nodes.title: Causal identification is conditional
nodes.statement: Unsupervised disentanglement is not generally identifiable; interventions can help under specified assumptions.

nodes.title: Causal abstraction concerns interventions
nodes.statement: Candidate scale changes should be tested for agreement on declared intervention predictions.

nodes.title: Reflection must face new evaluation
nodes.statement: Trace-based candidate search is promising but final evaluation must remain separate from adaptive selection.

nodes.title: Self-improvement guarantees are conditional
nodes.statement: Formal self-rewrite and incompleteness results do not imply a practical universally improving research agent.

nodes.title: Capability can reinforce control
nodes.statement: Capability gains may increase resources and access rights, which may support further capability growth.

nodes.title: Portability can distribute control
nodes.statement: Substitutable providers and portable representations may reduce dependence and concentrated veto rights.

nodes.title: Actions change prediction targets
nodes.statement: Using forecasts to select actions can alter the distribution of subsequent outcomes.

nodes.title: Exchange must separate delivery and settlement
nodes.statement: Offer order, latency, service quality, payment and reputation should be represented and evaluated separately.

nodes.title: Existence proofs do not establish truth
nodes.statement: A verified timestamp can support prior existence of committed bytes without proving their truth or availability to a model.

nodes.title: Encode text into graph with provenance
E4: Causal coordinates and mechanical hypotheses
Reviewed graph partition and merge execution record
Recorded graph partition and merge conformance
nodes.statement: The committed B2b run records 45/45 actual synthetic API checks, independent review, and a repaired repeated-identifier resource bound. It preserves strict graph-record collisions, ancestry and explicit cross-partition losses. This does not establish semantic equivalence, physical entity fission, external witnessing or predictive advantage.

nodes.title: Fresh control and exchange evidence with preserved corrections
nodes.statement: The B2b execution record describes four exact public-source captures and four current reported claims linked to byte spans. Two reviewed clarifications are superseding assertions, leaving earlier knowledge views intact. Captures use local collection time and do not reconstruct historical availability or establish source truth or market dominance. Raw external bytes are in a separate local store, not this bibliographic catalog.

nodes.title: SQLite FTS5 extension documentation
nodes.claim_supported: FTS5 provides full-text indexing, Unicode tokenization and built-in BM25 ranking, with numerically lower scores ranked first.
nodes.limitation: Retrieval ranking is not answer correctness or citation entailment; results depend on corpus, query and tokenizer configuration. Runtime and configuration must be recorded.

nodes.title: A maintained lexical baseline can use existing SQLite
nodes.statement: SQLite FTS5 supplies an existing full-text index and BM25 ranking for a local lexical retrieval baseline. It does not supply an evidence-grounded answer evaluator, historical eligibility rules or a sealed final cohort.

nodes.title: Reviewed atomic graph materialization execution record
Materialized outputs feed another fixed graph operation
nodes.statement: The committed B2c record reports atomic representations/manifests with full ancestry, 30/30 synthetic consumer checks, 308 passing tests and independent review. A reviewer exercised materialization followed by another transform and materialization. This establishes a checked local recursive consumer path, not learned improvement or semantic equivalence.

nodes.title: Logical transaction time must not backdate new evidence
nodes.statement: B2c review found that a shared transaction timestamp could make new observations or late forecasts appear earlier. The retained fix restricts grouped writes to derived records over existing evidence and requires fresh observations/questions/forecasts outside the group. Synthetic regressions verify this boundary; local collection time remains without independent witness.

nodes.title: Local retrieval reproduced across fresh processes
nodes.statement: The C1 run record reports two fresh lexical retrieval processes over four retained sources and twelve development queries with identical ordered result hashes. Source recall at one was 8/8, while full gold-span recall at five was 7/8. This is local retrospective development evidence, not sealed-cohort generalization, forecasting or independently witnessed execution.

nodes.title: Source selection does not establish evidence support
nodes.statement: The C1 record reports five of eight supported questions missing full gold support at rank one, one still missing at rank five, and all four unsupported questions returning related passages. No answers were generated. A post-hoc HTML text-node comparator is proposed; markup as a cause has not been experimentally established.

nodes.title: Actual retrieval evidence selects a bounded successor
nodes.statement: C2 validated and rescored both preserved C1 executions read-only, retained their exact inputs and metrics, and atomically selected a fixed representation comparison from the support-ranking gap. The run record reports 417 passing tests and independent review. This is a transparent priority rule, not a learned next-action policy or measured return on builder effort.

nodes.title: Fixed raw and HTML retrieval comparison protocol
Compare two fixed indexes under unchanged raw-span scoring
Python HTMLParser: callbacks, source positions and matching limits
nodes.claim_supported: The parser exposes callback positions and does not validate matching end tags; a static extractor must declare its own exclusion and source-mapping rules.
nodes.limitation: Mutable live documentation; this catalog entry is bibliographic, not an archived historical parser implementation or proof of browser visibility.

nodes.title: Static text extraction needs an explicit mapping contract
nodes.statement: HTMLParser callbacks and source positions support a declared static text projection, but matching-tag behavior and browser visibility are not supplied by that interface. The C3 protocol therefore fixes exclusions, entity handling, raw byte maps and empty-row preservation; it does not claim rendered visibility or semantic answerability.

nodes.title: Measured raw/HTML representation comparison and coverage handoff
Fixed HTML projection did not improve supporting-passage recall
nodes.statement: The C3 record reports four fresh reproduced runs over the frozen four-source development corpus. HTML text projection preserved span recall at 1/3/5 but reduced source recall at 1 from 8/8 to 7/8 and worsened source/span reciprocal rank. All four unsupported requests still returned passages. Raw remains the baseline and the controller selected fresh coverage. This is a development-specific result, not a general verdict on extraction or representation theory.

nodes.title: An exact runtime gate refused the wrong interpreter before search
nodes.statement: C3 preflight detected that an unqualified Python command selected a different Python/Unicode/SQLite runtime. It refused before creating an evidence fork or executing retrieval. The preserved original interpreter was verified, the complete suite rerun, and a new freeze linked to the retained refusal. This is a local recovery observation, not independent execution or timestamp assurance.
